brief: in-world library: books, notes, inscriptions and the unreliable written record
gap: RI-UIX05 D fails on content: book:item word ratio 1.57 vs bar >=15; game/data/books/ holds 1930 words across 7 texts
outputs_expected: corpus/80-methods/book-stats.py (named by RI-LOR03 method 1, DOES NOT EXIST)
tools/analysis/book-budget.mjs (RI-UIX05 method 7 flags do not exist on content-stats.mjs)
findings: DENOMINATOR MEASURED: item `description` words across game/data/items/**  = 1231 across 44 records. game/data/weapons/** contributes 0 `description` fields. Book words 1930 / 1231 = 1.5678 -> this is exactly the 1.57 in the brief, so the ratio's denominator is confirmed to be the `description` field and nothing else. Bar >=15 therefore needs >= 18,465 book words.
PHANTOM TOOL 1: RI-LOR03 Comparison method step 1 names `python3 corpus/80-methods/book-stats.py`. It does not exist on disk. TOOL-LOOP rule 1 applies.

PHANTOM FLAGS: RI-UIX05 method step 7 names `content-stats.mjs --books --items --dialogue --corroborate`. content-stats.mjs exists but implements NONE of those four flags (its USAGE lists only --data/--out/--json/--verbose/--help) and computes NO row of the SS D budget: no book:item ratio, no corroboration rate, no contradiction count, no direction count, no read-before-quest count. The flags are silently ignored, which is the exact `cmb-reach.mjs --verify` failure TOOL-LOOP rule 3.5 names.

ENGINE LOADER (game/src/engine.js:1887): books/*.json are loaded either as `elder-souls/book@1` (one doc, needs top-level `id`) or `@2` (doc with a `books` array). Both forms are keyed by `b.id`. Adding group files is safe.

READING SCREEN renders ONLY title, author and text (game/src/ui/screens/text.js drawBook). Metadata fields on a book record are never displayed, so registry fields (contradicts/taxon/wrong_on_purpose) cannot violate RI-UIX05 R8.

PAGINATION IS PURE JS: bookPagination()/bookLayout() in game/src/ui/screens/text.js depend only on the vector glyph tables in game/src/ui/glyphs.js. Words-per-page for EVERY book is therefore computable in bare Node with no browser, which is what RI-UIX05 method step 2 wanted a browser for.

EIGHT BOOK IDS ARE REFERENCED BY SHIPPED QUESTS AND DO NOT EXIST: book_the_seventh_recension + book_against_the_ninth_clause (mainline-act1 Q-MAIN-05 revealed_by), book_for_the_ninth_clause (mainline-act2 Q-MAIN-09), book_the_leave_book_of_thorn (mainline-act4), book_the_court_and_the_tide (blackmarsh-coast res_seal requires.knowledge), book_the_rootless_egg (blackmarsh-coast res_rootkeepers requires.knowledge), book_the_sap_and_the_knife (blackmarsh-core res_broker requires.knowledge). Three of those gate a non-violent quest resolution outright.

THREE BOOKS ARE NAMED AS EVIDENCE BY SEALED MYSTERIES M-01/M-02/M-03 and do not exist: book:on-the-tally-stones, book:the-oliis-bargain, book:valus-survey-fragment. Their leak_ngrams are recorded in corpus/50-world/sealed/SEALED-ANSWERS.md and must NOT appear in the book text.

RI-LOR03 SS3's seven exemplars were written to ship (`Exemplars 1, 2, 4 and 6 are intended to ship`) and are named as in_world_sources by canon-facts.json (CF-D001 A and B, CF-062, CF-006). They exist only in the corpus markdown, not in game/data. Shipping them closes the registry's dangling in_world_sources.
MAINLINE UA-02 declares `answered_in_a_book: true` for 'what was the reservoir built to do', requiring TWO in-world texts giving incompatible accounts. Neither existed.
RI-LOR03 method 1 fail bands: median < 350 words, p90 < 1200, < 3 multi-volume series, > 20% of books under 150 words. The last one bounds how many scraps the short tail may carry.

CORPUS SHAPE REACHED: 63 texts, 36,037 words, book:item ratio 29.27 (bar >=15, was 1.57). p10 113 / p25 216 / median 588 / p75 797 / p90 1264 / max 1512. Under-150 texts 11/63 = 17.5% (RI-LOR03 method 1 fails above 20%). Argonian-authored 17 (bar >=14). Three multi-volume series: the-drowned-tally (vols 4/6/11), the-stone-nests (I/II/III), a-progress-through-the-southern-marsh (I/II/III).

ID COLLISION CAUGHT: `what-the-water-took` already existed in interface-readables.json (Waneela of Lilmoth on the ford). The engine keys books by b.id in a Map, so a duplicate silently wins. Renamed the new Flu folk-tale to `what-the-water-went-round`. Any book tool must check for duplicate ids across files.
